title: Steady-state slew-rate prober and latency-heatmap serializer
author: Aisha Patel
commits: initial: add slew-rate prober harness and config schema
perf: implement steady-state detector and adaptive sampling window
report: heatmap serializer and compact binary layout for telemetry export
tests: add synthetic microburst scenarios and unit tests for detector
docs: usage + tuning guide for slew-rate thresholds
fix: tighten thread-safety around sample buffer access
description: Context: Production traffic exhibits sudden arrival-rate changes that current benchmarks treat as either isolated spikes or steady-state; we lacked a lightweight prober to characterize slew (rate-of-change) and to mark steady-state windows for downstream aggregations. This PR introduces a 'slew-rate prober' that emits time-series markers and a compact latency-heatmap serializer to efficiently export per-window histograms for postprocessing. Motivation: Provide an automated way to (1) detect sustained ramp-up/down phases, (2) isolate true steady-state windows for p95/p99 comparison across builds, and (3) export telemetry in a bandwidth-efficient format so long-run batch analyses are cheaper. High-level changes: added a new python prober harness (slew_rate_prober.py) with a configurable EWMA-based slew estimator and a hysteresis-driven steady-state detector; implemented adaptive sampling that reduces per-sample overhead during stable windows; added a Go-based heatmap_serializer that packs per-bucket counts into a compact TLV-like binary for faster ingestion by the analytics pipeline; added unit/integration tests and a tuning doc. Checklist: - [x] implement detector and sampling - [x] unit tests for detector edge cases - [x] create synthetic workloads (microburst/sustained-ramp) - [x] serializer with compatible schema - [x] docs and example config - [x] basic CI coverage and flake checks Backwards compatibility: The prober is opt-in and the serializer supports both new compact binary and legacy JSON exports via a feature flag in configs. Performance: local microbenchmarks show the prober adds <1% CPU overhead at 10k RPS on a c5.4xlarge equivalent and reduces exported telemetry size by ~6x versus naive JSON histograms. Risks & mitigations: false-positive steady-state detection on oscillatory traffic; mitigated by tunable hysteresis and a minimum-window-duration guard. Related work: follows ideas from ENG-3245 (steady-state isolation) and complements ENG-3310 (heatmap ingestion pipeline).

release_notes: Add opt-in slew-rate prober to detect ramp phases and export compact latency heatmaps; reduces telemetry size and improves steady-state isolation for performance comparisons.
